headline: High: shared MCP and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risk; OpenBB’s local-only network limits reduce but do not remove the pairwise hazard.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher can call MCP and ingest files/web content, while OpenBBTerminal uses MCP and a connect-once/consume-everywhere pattern. That creates a plausible bridge for attacker-controlled content to flow from A into B’s tool context. No direct shared channel is documented, so I choose medium rather than low because the interaction exists in default-style integrations.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher forwards untrusted web text into an MCP tool call consumed by OpenBBTerminal
IF both agents are connected to the same MCP server without provenance filtering
mitigations: Disable MCP between the agents for the session
Add a provenance tag to all A outputs before B reads them
Restrict B to read-only MCP endpoints
Manually inspect any A-generated instructions before passing them to B

B_data_leakage.rationale: A reads local documents and handles secrets such as API keys; B touches financial and licensed data and can use MCP/REST APIs. If they share a workspace or MCP backend, sensitive material from A can be exposed to B’s outputs or downstream APIs. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so uncertainty keeps this at medium, not high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or MCP data source
IF A’s research artifacts include secrets or local documents that B can read through a shared integration
mitigations: Separate workspaces for A and B
Remove secrets from any shared folder before running B
Disable API/REST export from B during the run
Use a throwaway MCP server with no file access

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has broad filesystem and network capabilities, while B cannot write files, modify git, or use network egress. The overlap is mostly one-way and does not show a direct write-write conflict. Because the profiles do not document a shared mutable resource, the conflict risk is limited and low.
conditions: IF both agents are given the same writable project directory through an external orchestrator
IF B is wrapped by a host process that adds write or git permissions not shown in the profile
mitigations: Keep B in a read-only environment
Run A and B in separate directories
Avoid shared git branches during the session
Confirm the orchestrator does not add hidden write permissions

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces research reports and citations, and B is a financial-modeling agent that can consume APIs and act on inputs. That makes it plausible for B to treat A’s output as authoritative unless an explicit verification step is inserted. The pairwise pathway is documented by the profiles, but not directly observed, so medium fits.
conditions: IF B ingests A’s report without a validation step
IF A’s citations or claims are used as inputs to B’s calculations or API calls
mitigations: Require B to re-check every factual claim from A
Pass only structured data, not prose, from A to B
Add a human review gate before B acts on A outputs
Log source URLs alongside each claim

E_compliance.rationale: A handles local documents, citations, and multiple external APIs; B handles financial and licensed data and exposes REST/MCP interfaces. The profiles do not specify residency or retention, but the mixed data classes and external API surfaces create a plausible compliance mismatch if regulated or licensed data crosses between them. I cannot prove a breach, so medium is the higher justified choice.
conditions: IF regulated financial or licensed data from B is mixed into A’s research artifacts
IF either agent stores or forwards data under a retention policy different from the source system
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of A’s research corpus
Document retention for both agents before the run
Use separate storage locations for licensed and public data
Review API destinations for residency constraints
